chapter_theme: Virtue's power: nothing brings more gain, and forgetting it is the worst loss. The chapter defines it inwardly, as a clean mind free of four faults, and presses that it must be practised now and continually.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar divides the chapter: nothing surpasses it (31), the harm of neglect (32), how it is practised (33), its nature (34-35), practising it while the body lasts (36), proof (37), its fruit of release (38), its fruit of joy and renown (39), and what must be done and avoided (40).

31.reading: It yields distinction and it yields wealth: what gain is greater for a living being than virtue?
31.nuance: The appeal is to self-interest, as virtue is praised for what it brings. Parimelazhagar takes சிறப்பு as release and செல்வம் as heaven, while Manakkudavar takes the second more plainly as wealth and sees the verse as answering those who say prosperity comes from wealth.

32.reading: No gain surpasses virtue, and no ruin surpasses forgetting it.
32.nuance: The opposite of virtue here is மறத்தல், forgetting, not doing wrong. Ruin comes through inattention, so the danger is ordinary.

33.reading: As far as you are able, without stopping, do the work of virtue wherever it can go.
33.nuance: ஒல்லும் வகையான் sets the measure by capacity, so the demand is relentless in duration but not impossible in scale. Parimelazhagar gives 'wherever' as mind, speech and body, while Kalaignar turns it into a requirement that all one's acts be virtuous.

34.reading: To be spotless in mind is the whole of virtue, and everything else is noisy show.
34.nuance: ஆகுல means clamour, so the charge against outward virtue is that it wants an audience. Parimelazhagar reads the verse with 33, so it concerns the mind of someone already doing good, not the mind in place of deeds. Manakkudavar's comment says the four faults were named earlier, which implies his text placed 35 before this verse.

35.reading: Virtue is what proceeds without slipping into these four: envy, craving, anger and harsh speech.
35.nuance: Virtue is defined by exclusion. The verse only lists the faults, and Parimelazhagar supplies a causal chain in which craving leads to anger and anger to harsh speech. Three of the four are inward and one is spoken.

36.reading: Do virtue without saying 'we'll see to it later': when you perish, it is a companion that doesn't perish.
36.nuance: The pun பொன்றுங்கால் பொன்றா turns on one verb: you perish and it doesn't. The verse doesn't say how virtue survives, and that is where the commentators part.

positions.position: When the body dies, virtue stays joined to the soul and travels into the next body.
positions.quote: செய்த உடம்பு அழியவும் உயிரோடு ஒன்றி ஏனை உடம்பினுட் சேறலின்

positions.position: Virtue survives as lasting renown after death.
positions.quote: அது ஒருவர் இறந்தபின் கூட அழியாப் புகழாய் நிலைத்துத் துணை நிற்கும்.

37.reading: There is no need to say 'this is the way of virtue': look between the one who bears the palanquin and the one who rides in it.
37.nuance: The couplet is very compressed, and it never says what difference we are to see. Taken at face value, it treats social rank as visible evidence of moral merit, which is one of the harder claims in the book.

positions.position: Rider and bearer are direct perceptual evidence of virtue's fruit, so scripture needn't be cited.
positions.quote: சிவிகையைக் காவுவானோடு செலுத்துவானிடைக் காட்சியளவை தன்னானே உணரப்படும்.

positions.position: This is an analogy of attitude: the virtuous ride through joy and sorrow lightly, and others carry life as a burden.
positions.quote: வாழ்க்கையில் வரும் இன்ப துன்பங்கள் இரண்டையும் எளியவாகக் கருதி மகிழ்வுடன் பயணத்தை மேற்கொள்வார்கள்.

38.reading: If you do good so that no day falls away unused, that is a stone blocking the road of your days.
38.nuance: வீழ்நாள் and வாழ்நாள் are set against each other, so fallen days are contrasted with living days. The stone's job depends entirely on what வாழ்நாள் means here.

positions.position: The stone blocks the road by which embodied days would return, which means it ends rebirth.
positions.quote: அச்செயல் அவன் யாக்கையோடு கூடும் நாள் வரும் வழியை வாராமல் அடைக்குங் கல்லாம்.

positions.position: The stone is a paving stone that smooths the road of this life.
positions.quote: வாழ்க்கைப் பாதையைச் சீராக்கி அமைத்துத் தரும் கல்லாக

39.reading: Only what comes through virtue is joy; everything else lies outside it and has no renown either.
39.nuance: Pope's gloss restricts this to 'domestic virtue', which follows Parimelazhagar and is not in the Tamil. The verse has a strong implication: joy is not separate from virtue and can't be got apart from it.

positions.position: The joy is sensual enjoyment that accords with household life; illicit pleasure turns to pain.
All enjoyment of any kind comes through virtue.
positions.quote: இஃது எல்லாப் போக நுகர்ச்சியும் இதனானே வருமென்றது.

positions.position: The joy arises from the renown a virtuous life brings.
positions.quote: அறவழி வாழ்க்கையில் வருகின்ற புகழால் ஏற்படுவதே இன்பமாகும்.

40.reading: What a person should do is virtue, and what a person should escape is blame.
40.nuance: Virtue's counterpart here is பழி, blame, not sin. Parimelazhagar explains it as what is blamed, and takes it to mean bad deeds. The term gives virtue a social measure as well as a cosmic one.

links.note: Here outward virtue is noise if the mind is stained. In 280, a shaven head and matted hair are unnecessary if one avoids what the world condemns. Note that 280 keeps the world's blame as the test, so the inward standard of 34 isn't all that matters.
Both press virtue into the present against the delay of 'later'. 36 promises a companion, and 335 frightens with the hiccup that stops the tongue. Each uses a different motive for the same urgency.

On the commentators' reading, 37 treats the difference between rider and bearer as virtue made visible. In 972, birth is the same for all beings, and distinction comes from what one does, which still leaves open whether the palanquin bearer's lot is deserved.

source_issues: Manakkudavar is not aligned for verses 32, 33, 35 and 37. His comment on verse 34 refers to the four faults as already stated, which suggests a different verse order in his text.
